title: LED fade in Rust. duty is a u8 at 5. What do these lines print?
options: It panics in debug and release
explain: saturating_sub stops at 0. wrapping_sub goes around: 5 - 10 = 251 for u8. Pick the one that matches what the hardware needs. A fade must stop at 0, so use saturating_sub.

title: Sensor packet for UART. On a 32-bit MCU or PC, what is sizeof(Packet)?
explain: uint16_t needs 2-byte alignment. The compiler adds 1 padding byte after id and 1 after the last byte, so the size is 6 and not 4. Never send a struct raw over UART. Write each field to the buffer, or use a packed struct and know its cost.

title: 9 V battery, a reverse-polarity diode (0.7 V drop), then the 7805. Load = 100 mA at 5 V. How much power does the 7805 burn?
explain: The diode drops 0.7 V, so the 7805 gets 8.3 V. It burns (8.3 - 5) x 0.1 A = 0.33 W. Without the diode it would burn 0.4 W. A series diode helps the heat a little and protects from a reversed battery.

title: You filter ADC noise with R = 10 kΩ and C = 100 nF. What is the cutoff frequency f = 1 / (2πRC)?
explain: 2π x 10 000 x 0.0000001 = 0.00628, so f = 159 Hz. Slow signals like TMP36 or a pot pass. Fast noise above this goes down. Also check that the divider source impedance (10 kΩ) is fine for the ADC.

title: The LED turns off at once after the press, not after 2 s. Tap the bug.
explain: t0 is never set when the state changes. It stays 0 (or an old time), so now - t0 is already big. Save the time at the moment you enter WAIT. Also run the timeout check in the else branch or the next call.

title: Sometimes loop() reads an old byte from the UART ring buffer. Tap the bug.
explain: The ISR moves head first and stores the byte after. If the ISR is still between the two lines when loop() runs, it sees head moved and reads the old byte. Store the data first, then publish the new head. The reader only sees complete entries.

title: STM32F4 USART. The ORE (overrun) flag is set and the RX interrupt fires again and again. How do you clear ORE?
explain: On STM32F4, ORE is cleared by a sequence: read USART_SR, then read USART_DR. Not every flag is write-1-to-clear (like EXTI->PR). Check the reference manual for each flag.

title: m = 0x68 is a mask of pressed buttons. What does the code print?
explain: m - 1 flips the lowest set bit and all bits under it: 0x68 - 1 = 0x67. The AND with m clears the lowest set bit: 0x68 & 0x67 = 0x60. Repeat it until 0 to count the buttons or to handle them one by one.

title: Uno with 2 KB SRAM. loop() builds messages with the Arduino String class (s += ...). It works for minutes, then crashes at random. Most likely cause?
options: The String class is too slow
explain: String allocates and frees small blocks on the heap. After many cycles the free space is split into holes, and one allocation fails or the heap meets the stack. Use fixed char buffers with snprintf instead.

pr.title: Fix timeout after the tick counter wraps
pr.author: dev
pr.body: The old check failed when the 32-bit tick counter wrapped. Use wrapping_sub.

explain: Good fix. The elapsed time is the difference, computed with wrap-around, so it stays right after the counter wraps. The old start + timeout could overflow (a panic in debug) and compare wrong. Same rule as millis() in C.
